ownership and native signed/x87/stack/callback ABI): Cdecl one FLOAT32 argument, void. Load input, divide by original PE DOUBLE255.0, FSTP DWORD local (explicit FLOAT32 rounding),

UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-11-11; original PE bytes, fresh disassembly, queue/history ownership, smoke lifetime, cutter registry, native region constraints and corrected stack/AL ABI): 
Cdecl(point3f*,INOUT operation100*,BYTE apply_hardness), returns AL0/1. Native reads only three stack args [EBP+8/+12/+16], both callers push3/pop12; no incoming x87 value is
consumed as a formal parameter. Typed the two pointer arguments and the byte mode from native field access. The old containment helper signature could cause decompiler inference of
a phantom ST0 argument here; do not treat that transient inferred register argument as native ABI. Clears op constraint vectors76/88 immediately; failures below can leave partially
mutated vectors/flags with no rollback. Scans region registry in order, admits through contains_point(point,region). No enabled check here other than region shape helper; direction
BYTE+8 and ice BYTE+9 require EXACT1.
For directional regions, initial direction=raw matrix row1 at region+40, scalar=FLOAT+12. With exactly one prior accepted direction, ordered dot(existing raw direction,new raw
direction)>double0.949999988079071 marks duplicate and skips adding it; equality/NaN does not merge. First accepted copies direction to op76, scalar to local EBP-4. Second copies
op88/local EBP-8 then requires dot(dir1,dir2)>=double-0.10000000149011612 OR unordered; ordered smaller rejects. With already two accepted directions, EVERY further directional
region increments count3 and rejects, even if parallel: duplicate test only ran at count1. Non-directional contained regions still contribute hardness/ice.
Maximum signed region hardness DWORD+4 starts-1; only strictly greater updates. If still-1 uses global hardness. Contained ice BYTE+9==1 ORs op.flags56 with0x10, never clears
previous ice. Only apply_hardness BYTE==1: exact hardness100 rejects; otherwise factor=F32(1-H/100), clamp[0,1], op.scale60=F32(oldScale*factor). H>100 becomes factor0 but is NOT
rejected by exact100 gate; negative values clamp factor1. Other apply bytes skip this scale/reject branch.
Unconditionally multiplies op76 by NEGATED local EBP-4 scalar and op88 by NEGATED EBP-8 scalar, then copies input point to op.position8. IMPORTANT: scalar locals are assigned only
for first/second accepted directions, respectively. Zero-direction path reads BOTH uninitialized stack locals; one-direction path still reads second uninitialized local, despite
clearing its vector first. Do not replace these native reads with defined scalar0 or assume missing constraints remain finite zero: arbitrary/NaN stack data can affect
multiplication. This is separate from the removed false x87 formal argument.
If accepted-direction count>0, computes up to two correction vectors initially zero by scanning saved count6FCCF4, records32 at6FCD00 and sidecars36 at6FDD50. Stops at next record
once correction1 nonzero for count1, or BOTH nonzero for count2. Saved first sidecar constraint+12 must be nonzero; second+24 adds a second candidate plane. Does NOT require
matching saved cutter id/room/flags. Radius gate uses CURRENT operation cutter's radius96 * SAVED record scale28, roundedF32 then square roundedF32, strictly ORDERED greater than
F32 distanceSquared(saved sidecar origin,input point). No cutter NULL guard.
For each saved plane vector, normalize_get_length yields unit normal and original-length squared bound (F32 stores; helper fallback semantics retained). For each unmatched current
direction slot, normalize its scaled constraint vector. Admit alignment dot(normal,currentDirection)>=double0.95 OR unordered, AND dot(normal,normalize(point-savedOrigin)) strictly
ORDERED>0. Project ORIGINAL input point onto plane(normal,savedOrigin), require squared normal length strictly ORDERED>distanceSquared(projected,input). Store
correction=projected-input into its slot. Then append correction1 followed by correction2 to op.position8. Not nearest-plane selection: first nonzero correction for each slot
sticks; zero correction remains an unfilled sentinel and may be replaced. No iterative re-projection using already shifted position, finite validation or all-or-nothing failure

comments:
UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-11-11; original PE bytes, fresh disassembly, RFL volume/decal layouts, cumulative corner room queries, mover list and auxiliary-node ownership, linked physics flags and native debug draw arguments): 
Cdecl(center3f,matrix3 rows,dimensions3f), returns first nonnull room pointer orNULL. Copies center to local scratch and queries
world_resolve_cached_room(world,NULL,zeroVector,point,0). With NULL prior-room delegate performs endpoint room lookup, so start zeroVector does not imply movement from origin or
ray intersection. Center hit returns immediately.
If center misses, first corner is center -row0*(dimX/2) +row1*(dimY/2) -row2*(dimZ/2), with half-products stored binary32 and vector operations materialized individually. Queries
that corner, then cumulatively adds +row0*X,-row1*Y,-row0*X,+row2*Z,+row1*Y,+row0*X,-row1*Y, querying after EVERY step. Thus center then eight corners in sign
order(-,+,-),(+,+,-),(+,-,-),(-,-,-),(-,-,+),(-,+,+),(+,+,+),(+,-,+). Each step starts from previous rounded corner, not a freshly reconstructed center expression.
Returns first room in that order; does not require all points in same room or perform full box/world-overlap test. Does not change input center/matrix/dimensions, normalize basis,
clamp dimensions, checkNULL inputs/world or project a decal itself. Room-query delegates may update their own scratch.

flags+8 mask0xF0000 is set. Let q=length_squared(particle_position-region_position+12),R2=region+60,strength=region+100. Region bit4 takes priority and scales direction by
F32((1-q/R2)*strength); else bit8 scales by F32(q/R2*strength); otherwise strength alone. No attenuation clamp or R2-zero guard. Adds this acceleration*global frame delta to
velocity, or uses global ambient acceleration when no region; then adds updated velocity*delta to position. No collision sweep, emitter ownership, lifetime, or per-record age.
Point inside strict ordered camera box: scratch0x872A48 becomes particle_position-view_position. Outside: if ordered velocity_length_squared>1 divides velocity by its SQUARED
length, not its length. Selects rand()%6 cube face (+X,-X,+Y,-Y,+Z,-Z), fixes that offset component at +/-radius0x662E0C, samples other two uniformly within that range, stores
offset in scratch0x872A48 and respawns position=view_position+offset. No liquid recheck before this relocation; liquid admission occurs below.
Rendering requires ordered dot(scratch,view_forward)>0 and particle point in the SAME view room's liquid. Set d2=F32(length_squared(scratch)); native d2>=1 OR unordered passes its
threshold. For ordered1<=d2<5 alpha factor is F32(d2/5); at d2>=5 OR unordered factor=F32(1-d2/max(d2,global squared cutoff0x872A70)). Note thresholds1/5 are squared distances, not

PAUSE semantics are stateful: skips the entire per-record motion/respawn/scratch update but still performs dot/liquid/distance/alpha/render for each record. The shared scratch

state is left modified. Unwind entries only clear static guard bits; no per-call particle allocation or cleanup.

Version>=167 reads serialized normal XYZ plus float d before texture fields (546877..5468A1); finalization receives that four-float plane at546B30. Sets byte 1DAEE4C as a one-shot/reentrancy latch and never clears it, including on file-open failure. Derives executable basename without extension for the report title, replaces its filename component with errorlog.txt, opens with OPEN_ALWAYS/no sharing/write-through, seeks to end, and appends the report. and flushing its 1000-byte buffer past a 950-byte threshold. Closes file and returns 0, also on duplicate/error paths; it is an exception filter result, not a success indicator. UNREALRED VERIFIED [nonworld-byte-rgb-20260903]: Mesh-face submission consumer for the decoded RGB8 paths. It computes ambient/diffuse vertex bytes with 0x0052A000, requests specular bytes from 0x0052A1E0 when material field +0x84 is positive, and—when that helper's point-hit flag is set—emits a separate pass whose alpha is the arithmetic mean of specular R, G, and B.

UNREALRED VERIFIED [self-illumination-20260903]: After ordinary non-world diffuse lighting, evaluates material self-illumination, computes round(255*value), and raises each vertex RGB byte independently to at least that common floor. Material type 2 then modulates the resulting RGB by its per-channel bytes at +0x09..+0x0B.
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-animation-20260903]: Evaluates material alpha once per face and multiplies it into all pass alpha. Type 0 submits one selected texture frame; type 1 binds and submits slot 0 at weight 1-crossfade, then slot 1 at crossfade; type 2 submits vertex color without a texture. Texture-slot frame selection uses each slot's start, speed, and playback mode.
UNREALRED VERIFIED [reflection-binding-20260903]: Corrected reflection texture lifetime: material +0xB4 is only a positive presence gate. The reflection branch never passes or selects that handle; immediate drawing binds stage 0 from pending primary handle 0x0187CCE8, left by the last base-slot bind (slot 0 for type 0, slot 1 for type 1, and potentially prior state for untextured type 2). This is retail behavior, not an inferred environment-map bind.
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-type2-tint-20260903]: Material type 2 is untextured and submits the computed vertex RGB8. After diffuse lighting and the self-illumination byte floor, it multiplies R/G/B independently by unsigned material bytes +0x09/+0x0A/+0x0B, divides each product by 255, truncates toward zero, and stores the low byte.
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-alpha-byte-20260903]: Evaluates the clamped material alpha once per face, then rounds each effective pass alpha to RGB8. Type 0 and type 2 use round(alpha*255); type 1 independently rounds alpha*255*(1-crossfade) and alpha*255*crossfade. The specular pass uses round(alpha*255), while reflection uses round(reflection_amount*alpha*255).
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-type1-vertex-weight-20260903]: Type 1 evaluates one clamped crossfade w, then constructs two separate textured passes. For every vertex it multiplies each already-lit unsigned RGB8 channel by 1-w for slot 0 and by w for slot 1, forces x87 truncation toward zero, and stores the low byte before each slot is submitted.
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-type1-pass-composition-20260903]: Type 1 submits slot 0 before slot 1. Each slot receives an independently rounded global alpha byte, round(material_alpha*255*(1-w)) then round(material_alpha*255*w). Non-additive slots select blend mode 3 (source alpha over inverse source alpha on the normal device path), while material flag +8 selects blend mode 2 (source alpha over one) for both slots.
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-type1-source-over-color-20260903]: Type 1 submits slot 0 then slot 1 with packet flags 5. Each source RGB is texture times its independently truncated weighted vertex RGB; each source alpha is its independently rounded renderer alpha, additionally multiplied by texture alpha only for alpha-bearing textures. Non-additive framebuffer composition is ordered source-over.
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-type1-additive-composition-20260903]: Material type 1 with flag +8 submits slot 0 then slot 1 through the same additive state. Each slot has independently truncated weighted vertex RGB and independently rounded global alpha. The framebuffer result is D + S0*A0 + S1*A1, with texture alpha included in each Ai for alpha-bearing textures.
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-type1-additive-depth-20260903]: Material type 1 with flag +8 loads the same fixed packed state at 0x0187CC60 for slot 0 and slot 1. There is no alternate per-section depth-state selection inside either additive branch.
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-type2-alpha-ownership-20260903]: Material type 2 rounds materialAlpha*255, publishes that byte as current renderer alpha with white current RGB, then submits its independently tinted vertex RGB using packet flags 4 and the untextured state at 0x0187CD30. Base-pass coverage therefore owns material alpha only, not vertex or texture alpha.
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-type2-fixed-state-20260903]: The material-type dispatch routes type 2 directly to an immediate base submission using flags 4 and the immutable packed state at 0x0187CD30. The type-2 base pass therefore cannot inherit generic additive or no-depth section presentation flags.
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-type1-source-over-depth-20260903]: For each non-additive type-1 slot, texture alpha selects state 0x0187CC50 and opaque texture selects 0x0187CC8C. Both fixed states use source-over blend selector 3 and depth selector 4; no section-level no-depth selector participates.
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-type0-alpha-ownership-20260903]: Material type 0 rounds materialAlpha*255 into current renderer alpha, then every textured LOD-override, additive, alpha-texture, or opaque-texture branch submits packet flags 5. Coverage owns material alpha and, where alpha selector 3 applies, texture alpha; no branch admits vertex alpha.
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-type0-fixed-state-20260903]: Material type 0 first gives mesh LOD flag 0x8 priority, forcing source-over state (1,2,3,3,1,0). Otherwise material additive byte +8 selects (1,2,3,2,1,3); an alpha texture selects (1,2,3,3,5,0); and an opaque texture selects (1,2,0,3,4,0).
UNREALRED VERIFIED [material-type0-alpha-test-threshold-20260903]: Only ordinary material type 0 with a texture classified as alpha-bearing dynamically packs depth/alpha selector 5. LOD-override, additive, and opaque-texture branches select other fixed states.

VERIFIED [world-light-fog-clip]: Emits base world geometry before projected dynamic-light geometry. Base packets apply each group's packed descriptor at 0x5E88A6 and draw at 0x5E96C6; the projected pass then selects fog-mode-3 state and draws at 0x5EA9E4, so an enabled base fog does not attenuate or tint the later additive contribution. name: rf_jpeg_prep_pre_process_data
stored_type: unsigned int __cdecl(_DWORD *, int, unsigned int *, unsigned int, int, unsigned int *, unsigned int)
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcprepct.c:pre_process_data matched): Seven-argument preprocessing callback. Converts input rows into the color buffer, updating input count, next_buf_row and rows_to_go. Each full max_v group is downsampled into the next output row group. At image end, repeats the final converted row to complete a group, then repeats the last output row per component to fill the requested output group capacity. Row counts are integers; the old pointer inference in the padding helper was incorrect.

name: rf_jpeg_prep_expand_bottom_edge

comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcprepct.c:expand_bottom_edge matched): void(rowPointerArray, unsigned numCols, int inputRows, int outputRows). Copies numCols bytes from the LAST ORIGINAL row (inputRows-1) into each row inputRows..outputRows-1 using jcopy_sample_rows. No action when inputRows >= outputRows. No inputRows > 0 or capacity check. The third argument is an integer row count, not void **.

name: rf_jpeg_prep_pre_process_context
stored_type: int __cdecl(size_t *, int, unsigned int *, unsigned int, int, unsigned int *, unsigned int)
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcprepct.c:pre_process_context matched): Context preprocessing callback using a ring of 3*max_v actual rows plus aliased pointer margins. Initially fills two groups, replicating the first row into negative context indices. At image end, repeats the last row to the next stop. Downsamples this_row_group when ready, advances by max_v and wraps at 3*max_v. If input ends before the image is complete, returns to await more input. Provides the neighboring rows required by smoothing.

name: rf_jpeg_prep_create_context_buffer
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcprepct.c:create_context_buffer matched): Allocates 5*max_v row pointers per component and 3*max_v actual sample rows. Middle pointer groups address the actual rows; the leading group aliases the last actual group and the trailing group aliases the first. Stores a pointer shifted past the leading margin, permitting negative context row indices. Sample width is max_h*8*width_in_blocks/h_samp. Pixels are initialized later by preprocessing.

name: rf_jpeg_jinit_downsampler
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcsample.c:jinit_downsampler matched): Initializes the 52-byte downsampler at cinfo+352. Method pointers begin at +12; +8 is need_context_rows. CCIR601_sampling raises error 25. Chooses full-size, h2v1, h2v2, or generic integer-ratio methods; fractional ratios raise error 38. Smoothing selects the full-size or h2v2 smooth method and requests context rows. Unsupported smoothing for other ratios retains the ordinary method and emits trace 99 at level 0; supported components may still be smoothed.

name: rf_jpeg_downsample_start_pass
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcsample.c:start_pass_downsample matched): No-op start-pass callback with one unused cdecl cinfo argument. The old no-argument inferred prototype omitted this callback ABI argument.

name: rf_jpeg_downsample_dispatch_components
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcsample.c:sep_downsample matched): Dispatches each component to its selected downsampling method: (cinfo, component, inputRows[i]+inRowIndex, outputRows[i]+outRowGroupIndex*v_samp). Component records have an 84-byte stride. Row pointer offsets are scaled by four bytes.

name: rf_jpeg_downsample_integer_box
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcsample.c:int_downsample matched): Generic integer box downsampling. hExpand=max_h/h_samp, vExpand=max_v/v_samp, outputWidth=8*width_in_blocks. Pads the INPUT right edge to hExpand*outputWidth. Each output sample is (sum + area/2)/area over hExpand*vExpand pixels. Initializer guarantees positive integral sampling ratios.

name: rf_jpeg_downsample_expand_right_edge
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcsample.c:expand_right_edge matched): For each of numRows, repeats the byte at inputCols-1 into columns inputCols..outputCols-1. Nonpositive extension does nothing. Does not validate inputCols > 0 or destination capacity. Callers may use it on input or output rows.

name: rf_jpeg_downsample_fullsize
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcsample.c:fullsize_downsample matched): Copies max_v rows of image_width bytes to output, then pads the OUTPUT right edge to 8*width_in_blocks. Selected when component sampling equals the maximum in both axes. Does not modify input padding.

name: rf_jpeg_downsample_h2v1
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcsample.c:h2v1_downsample matched): Horizontal 2:1 downsampling. Pads INPUT rows to twice the output width, then computes (a+b+bias)>>1 for each pixel pair. Bias alternates 0/1 across columns and resets to zero each row. No vertical averaging or smoothing.

name: rf_jpeg_downsample_h2v2
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcsample.c:h2v2_downsample matched): Horizontal and vertical 2:1 downsampling. Pads INPUT rows to twice the output width; each output is the average of a 2x2 block using (sum+bias)>>2. Bias alternates 1/2 across columns and resets to one each output row.

name: rf_jpeg_downsample_h2v2_smooth
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcsample.c:h2v2_smooth_downsample matched): Integrated 2x2 downsampling and smoothing. Requires one context row above and below; right-pads rows -1..max_v to twice output width. With S=smoothing_factor, each central 2x2 pixel has weight 16384-80*S, four outer corner pixels have weight 16*S, and eight outer edge pixels have weight 32*S. Adds 32768 and shifts by 16 into a byte. Horizontal edges are replicated. No explicit S clamp.

name: rf_jpeg_downsample_fullsize_smooth
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jcsample.c:fullsize_smooth_downsample matched): Full-size 3x3 smoothing. Requires one context row above and below and pads their right edges. Center weight is 65536-512*S; each of eight neighbors has weight 64*S. Adds 32768 and shifts by 16 into a byte. Uses rolling column sums and replicates horizontal edges. Does not downsample or explicitly clamp S.

name: rf_jpeg_color_rgb_ycc_convert

name: rf_jpeg_color_rgb_gray_convert
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jccolor.c:rgb_gray_convert matched): Converts interleaved RGB rows to gray plane 0 using (19595*R+38470*G+7471*B+32768)>>16 through the lookup tables. name: rf_jpeg_color_cmyk_ycck_convert
comments: UNREALRED VERIFIED (2026-10-29; original PE bytes and fresh disassembly; IJG v6b jccolor.c:cmyk_ycck_convert matched): Converts interleaved CMYK to planar YCCK.
